name: Women's CAP dark blue polo, long sleeves, no pocket, worn out over a medium gray skirt (embroidery positions only)
size_basis: Silhouette traced from CAPR 39-1 Figure 5.5 (3 March 2020, p.80; base-art/ref_polo_CAPR_fig5-5.png, PDF page 108 rendered at 300 dpi, trace-polo.js: shirt-only mask, left half mirrored, Moore trace, RDP 1.1 px). Scale 0.03495 in per figure pixel: the same embroidered seal is 83.9 px across (equal-area circle) in this figure and 94.9 px (2.93 in) in the men's figure, so the women's figure is drawn 1.131 times larger on the page. ESTIMATE: the regulation gives no garment dimension and the figure is a schematic drawing (its waist, 11.1 in flat, is narrower than a real polo's; the Class B blouse sheet's is 12.2 in). Long sleeves: the arm below the short sleeve's end follows the Class B long-sleeve sheet's arm (class_b_female_long_outline.json, K-scaled) shifted to the polo's sleeve width; ESTIMATE. Colours sampled from the figure: shirt #001b52, belt #201a18, trousers #746f6c, skirt #86827e.
landmarks_note: rects are {x,y,w,h} (top-left); polygons are [[x,y]...]; all in user units (0.01 in), origin top-left of the artwork box. The *_slot entries that carry w_in / h_in are {x,y} = the CENTRE of the slot in user units, w_in / h_in in inches. seal_slot: embroidered CAP seal, wearer's RIGHT breast (the picture's left), w_in = the figure-measured seal (2.93 in; the insignia-cap-seal asset is 2.50 in, CAPR 39-1 Fig A6-4: the figure draws the polo seal larger, the engine places the asset at the slot centre). pen_pocket_slot: the tactical polo's pen pocket on the wearer's LEFT sleeve (the picture's right), {x,y} its centre, w_in x h_in its size (1.4 x 5.5 in, estimate), angle_deg the SVG rotate() that turns an upright box onto the sleeve's axis, flap_in the flap depth. name_slot: the embroidered name line on the wearer's LEFT breast, w_in = 4.2 in (the same line length as the men's sheet; Figure 5.5 draws a 3.3 in name), h_in = the figure's cap height. badge_slot: centre of the badge / duty title line, h_in 1.14 (the figure's badge), 1/2 in above the name_slot top (CAPR 39-1 5.3.2.1.1; the figure draws 0.65 in), w_in nominal. print_seal_slot: the screen-printed CAP seal (5.3.1.2) on the wearer's LEFT breast, the seal_slot mirrored about the centre line. collar_left / collar_right name the leaf on the PICTURE's left / right (as the Class B sheets do); shoulder_seam_right / left and every anchor named left / right are the WEARER's (right = the picture's left). hat_view {front, back}: where the cap assets hat-baseball-cap-blue and hat-baseball-cap-blue-back sit (their boxes, bottoms 0.25 in below the collar-tip line, the back view 0.5 in to the picture's right of the front); they lie above this artwork box. hat_attach: the collar-tip line on the centre line.

scale.basis: the same embroidered seal as the men's figure (94.9 px = 2.93 in there, 83.9 px here)

documented: dark blue knit polo shirt, short or long sleeves, embroidered CAP seal on the RIGHT breast; the female version has no pocket (females may wear either) (CAPR 39-1 5.3.1.1)
first and last name embroidered in white thread on the LEFT breast; one badge or duty title 1/2 in over the name; no grade insignia (5.3.1.1, 5.3.2, 5.3.2.1.1)
women may wear the shirt out; its length must not fall below mid-hip (5.3.1)
medium gray skirt, straight or A-line, slight flare, knee length (5.3.4); belt optional with belt loops (5.3.5)
assumed: garment dimensions (scale from the seal size, same in both figures)
no photograph of a real CAP polo was available offline (the charter forbids downloads): colours are sampled from Figure 5.5
collar leaf, placket, button, pocket, belt, loop and buckle geometry read off Figure 5.5 (pixel table FIG in make-polo.js)
seams, stitches and the ribbed cuff are shown as flat geometric lines, no knit texture
long sleeve below the short sleeve: arm profile of the Class B long-sleeve shirt sheet (same wearer), 2.5 in ribbed cuff (ESTIMATE)
skirt: figure edge widths, flared 0.55 in more by the crop line (5.3.4 slight flare); hem not drawn (cut off at the crop, as the Class B blouse sheet)
